prompt:
solution.py is meant to implement the specification below, but it contains several defects. One has been reported: `round_decimal("2.5", 0)` returns "3" instead of "2". Fix that and every other deviation from the specification. Keep the public names and signatures unchanged and do not change behaviour the specification requires.

Specification: Implement `round_decimal(text, places)` in solution.py: round a decimal number given as a string to `places` digits after the point using round-half-to-even, exactly, for inputs of any length (the result must not depend on binary floating point). Input syntax: an optional `-`, one or more digits, and optionally a `.` followed by one or more digits. Output: the same syntax with exactly `places` fraction digits (no point at all when `places` is 0), no leading zeros other than a single zero before the point, and no minus sign when the rounded value is zero. `places` is an int of at least 0; raise ValueError when it is negative. Raise ValueError for malformed input such as the empty string, `+1`, `.5`, `5.`, `1e3`, `1,5` or anything with spaces.
acceptance: ties go to the even digit
exact for inputs of any length
zero is written without a minus sign
a leading plus sign is rejected
